comments.author: Adrian Michalski
comments.comment: A practical stop condition I like is “budget plus evidence”: max steps/time/tool calls, but also a verifier that can point to the exact state change proving success. The tricky part is separating “agent is done” from “agent produced a plausible explanation of being done.” How do you usually calibrate the judge threshold before it starts blocking valid completions?

comments.author: Maximilian Roland Haberstroh
comments.comment:
800k+ LoC changes the game: the bottleneck is not coding speed, it is blast radius control. I would make evals, rollback paths, permission boundaries, and cost telemetry part of day-one onboarding, because agents amplify both good architecture and messy ownership fast.

What is the first guardrail you would put in place before giving agents merge access?

#AI #Engineering

comments.author: K&C (Krusche & Company)
comments.comment: The hard part is not installing a coding agent - it is defining the guardrails around repo context, test execution, and human review so speed does not turn into bigger diffs with hidden risk. Curious if you measure adoption by cycle time, escaped defects, or percentage of generated changes that survive review unchanged? #AgenticAI
